SEC-HD-V6-01.note: Head noun 'mat' is singular; no comma may separate subject from verb, so B is out by rule and D leaves the sentence verbless. Same shape as V6-24 and V6-17 (singular head buried under a modifier).

SEC-HD-V6-02.note: Nominative absolute; A and D are comma splices, C's comma turns the absolute into a stranded appositive with no predicate. Option cast (finite / -ing / comma+-ing) is the same as V6-21.

SEC-HD-V6-03.note: Proximity agreement with plural 'students' plus the past frame ('had no dissecting room') rules out B, C, D.

SEC-HD-V6-04.note: 'a third of the foragers' takes plural; B ('reverted') is number-neutral and fails only on tense consistency with the surrounding generic present ('can run', 'is damaged') - the weakest exclusion in the batch.

SEC-HD-V6-05.note: Clausal subject is singular; C and D leave the sentence without a main verb.

SEC-HD-V6-06.note: Comma closes the long 'Because...' clause; C's semicolon would follow a fragment, B brackets the subject, A omits the required comma.

SEC-HD-V6-07.note: Only 'wax' can be the thing secreted; B and D dangle, C is nonfinite.

SEC-HD-V6-08.note: BROKEN: A is fully grammatical. 'recorded the depth..., the character..., and how the tide sets, but they left out...' coordinates a nominal clause with two noun phrases - accepted by every usage authority (parallelism among nominals of different internal form is a preference, not a rule), and A carries the same correct comma before 'but'. Two conforming options.

SEC-HD-V6-09.note: 'Since that paper appeared' plus 'no surgeon now records' forces present perfect; head noun 'practice' is singular.

SEC-HD-V6-10.note: Two verbs drawing number from different nouns: relative-clause verb from plural 'the bees', main verb from singular 'The number'.

SEC-HD-V6-11.note: Dash must be closed with a dash, and the verb agrees with plural 'calls' across the supplement.

SEC-HD-V6-12.note: Semicolon joins two independent clauses; gerund 'turning' supplies the second subject. A, B and D are splices or leave 'took' subjectless.

SEC-HD-V6-13.note: 'Each of' is singular; C fails only on tense against the present-tense frame.

SEC-HD-V6-14.note: Embedded question keeps statement order; 'clams' is plural. A and B invert, B and C also misagree.

SEC-HD-V6-15.note: Two singular NPs joined by 'and' are plural; 'uses today' and the present-tense colon clause fix the tense.

SEC-HD-V6-16.note: Colon introduces a list of noun phrases; a semicolon requires an independent clause, B is a fragment, D misagrees with singular 'something'.

SEC-HD-V6-17.note: Singular 'The line' needs a finite main verb; A and C leave a fragment. Same construction as V6-01 and V6-05.

SEC-HD-V6-18.note: 'not because X but because Y' correlative; A breaks it and reverses the passage's logic, C leaves 'of the price ... was falling' ungrammatical. Number is settled by 'was falling', six words after the blank - just outside the four-word window but a real downstream tell for B.

SEC-HD-V6-19.note: DEFECT: the relative verb 'that work' sits two words after the blank and forces a plural subject, killing C without any reasoning about the passage. B (no comma before 'so') and D (dependent 'so that' clause after a semicolon) remain, so the tell narrows the field to two rather than giving the whole answer.

SEC-HD-V6-20.note: Third member of a series of infinitives must stay infinitival to match 'to keep' and 'to sound'.

SEC-HD-V6-21.note: Participial phrase after a complete clause; A and C are splices, D coordinates a participle with nothing. Option cast duplicates V6-02.

SEC-HD-V6-22.note: Fifteen-year span already under way at a stated past point ('in 1984') requires past perfect progressive; B and C also misagree with singular 'the number'.

SEC-HD-V6-23.note: Fused relative takes nominative case from its own clause, not from 'between'; C and D leave that clause nonfinite.

SEC-HD-V6-24.note: 'and' inside the of-phrase does not compound the subject; head is singular 'The nightly rise'. The coordinated 'and has never been counted' later in the sentence independently confirms the singular, and the singular predicate nominal 'the largest movement' three words after the blank is a soft hint in the same direction.
